UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2528 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 3rd AUGUST, 2026 
 
Filling up of Board-level positions in CPSEs 
 
2528. Shri Kali Charan Singh:                  
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of sanctioned and filled posts of Chairperson, Chairman and Managing 
Director (CMD), Managing Director, Functional Directors and Independent 
Directors as on 30 June 2026, Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSE)-wise; 
(b) the number of Board -level positions lying vacant for more than six months and 
more than one year, respectively; 
(c) whether meetings of the Boards, Audit Committees, CSR Committees and other 
statutory committees have been affected due to shortage of Independent 
Directors, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has fixed any timeline for completion of appointments 
through the appropriate selection process, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken to  ensure that prolonged vacancies do not adversely affect 
governance, investment decisions, project execution and the financial 
performance of CPSEs? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) and (b) : Public Enterprises Selection Board (PESB) is responsible for the 
selection and  recommendation of personnel to the posts of Chairman/CMD/MD 
(Level-I) and Functional Director (Level -II) in the CPSEs. The Government however, 
in some instances, may decide to fill a particular Board l evel post through modes 
other than PESB procedure such as Search -cum-Selection Committee (SCSC) 
procedure, on deputation basis, etc. or decide to keep particular Board level post(s) 
in abeyance. 
As per available information from PESB, in case of Board level posts in CPSEs being 
filled through PESB procedure, t here are 22 vacant posts of full -time functional 
Directors (7 posts of CMD/MD and 15 posts of functional Directors) in various 
CPSEs having date of vacancy prior to 30.07.2026. Of these 22 posts, only three 
posts are vacant for more than six months. PESB has already furnished its 
recommendations for other vacant Board level posts having date of vacancy prior to 
30.07.2026 for processing by the c oncerned administrative Ministry for 
approval/decision of the competent authority.  As per available information, presently 
75 positions of non -official (Independent) Directors are filled in various CPSEs as 
against the requirements of around 750 as per provisions of Companies Act, 2013 
and SEBI (LODR) Regulations.  The Search Committee has made recommendations 

 
 
for filling up around more 100 positions of non-official (Independent) Directors on the 
Boards of various CPSEs. 
(c) : The meetings of Board and Board Committees are required to be held as per 
relevant provisions of Companies Act, 2013 and/or SEBI (LODR) Regulations  which 
also inter alia prescribe the constitution of Board Committees. The CPSEs are 
independent Board-driven entities functioning under the administrative jurisdiction of 
the concerned Ministr ies/Departments. The Board of Directors of CPSE and 
concerned administrative Ministry/Department is required to ensure compliance with 
these provisions to ensure smooth functioning of Board and Board Committees.  
(d) and (e) : It has been the constant endeavour of the Government to ensure that 
Board level posts in the CPSEs are filled up as per extant procedure in a timely 
manner. The Government has issued timelines for processing of the proposals for 
appointment and extension/non-extension to Board level post s in CPSEs which inter 
alia provide that the administrative Ministries/Departments are required to initiate the 
job description (JD) for a post and communicate the same to PESB within the 
stipulated time i.e. three months in advance of the stipulated period of one year of 
the date of occurrence of  vacancy. If any Ministry/Department does not  forward the 
JD for a post to PESB within the  stipulated time, PESB initiates the JD one year  
before the occurrence of the vacancy and starts  consultation with the 
Ministry/Department so that  the selection process is started expeditiously.  To track 
the status of both existing and anticipated  vacancies and initiating timely action, 
PESB has developed a comprehensive  vacancy tracking  dashboard reflecting 
various milestones such as creation of vacancy, initiation of job description, 
advertising the post, screening/shortlisting the applications and convening the 
selection meetings. 
The Government has also issued guidelines regarding assignment of additional 
charge for manning vacant Board level posts in CPSEs so that regular functioning of 
CPSEs is not adversely affected.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2530 
ANSWERED ON 03/08/2026 
 
Setting up of state-of-the-art Software Park in Dhanbad 
 
†2530.  Shri Dulu Mahato: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that Dhanbad has prestigious institutes like Indian 
Institute of Technology (IIT-ISM), BIT Sindri and Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research 
(CSIR-CIMFR), from where thousands of technically skilled youth pass out every year, if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) whether these talented youths have to migrate to metropolitan cities like Bengaluru, Pune 
and Noida for employment due to lack of Information Technology (IT)/Software industry in 
Dhanbad, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to set up a state -of-the-art software park or 'Industry-
Academia Innovation Centre' in Dhanbad in coordination with the Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology under the National Education Policy; and 
(d) if so, the steps being taken by the Government in this direction to provide employment to 
local youth, foster startup culture and prevent brain drain? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 
(a) to (d):  In the state of Jharkhand, the Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines), 
Dhanbad [IIT (ISM) Dhanbad], originally established in 1926 as the Indian School of Mines, was 
accorded IIT status in 2016 through an Act of Parliament and is recognized as an  Institution of 
National Importance (INI). Further, other INIs including National Institute of Technology (NIT) 
Jamshedpur and I ndian Institute of Information Technology (I IIT) Ranchi have also been 
functioning in the state of Jharkhand. These institutes are known for their excellence in technical 

education, advanced research in both fundamental and applied domains, innovation, promotion 
of entrepreneurship, and consultancy services to industry. 
A significant number of alumni of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad are presently serving in reputed 
Central Public Sector Undertakings, State Government undertakings, and leading private sector 
organisations located across the country including in Dhanbad and other parts of Jharkhand. IIT 
(ISM), Dhanbad, through its incubation centres, has supported the incubation of 
approximately 150 startups, facilitating access to funding from various venture capital firms and 
government agencies. In addition, the Institute conducts  Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY) training programmes for local youth and faculty members from other institutions 
(Training of Trainers).  
 
At present, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad operates  four innovation and incubation centres  with 
support from various Ministries and Government agencies. The Institute has established a robust 
innovation ecosystem through its four incubation centres —Technology Innovatio n in 
Exploration & Mining Foundation (TexMin Foundation), CIIE IIT (ISM) Dhanbad Foundation, 
Atal Community Innovation Centre  (ACIC IIT( ISM) Dhanbad) , and the CIL Innovation 
&  Incubation Centre. These centres promote innovation, entrepreneurship, startu p incubation, 
industry–academia collaboration, technology commercialization, and skill development.  
 
The Birsa Institute of Technology, Sindri, is under the administrative control of the 
Government of Jharkhand. It currently offers Bachelor of Technology programmes in varied 
engineering disciplines. CSIR-Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research (CSIR -CIMFR), 
Dhanbad, a constituent laboratory of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), 
undertakes R&D activities across the entire coal -energy value chain, covering exploration, 
mining, and utilization. 
Software Technology Parks of India (STPI)  under the Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology (MeitY)  has established its centre at Dhanbad (Jharkhand).  STPI 
Dhanbad has been developed with state-of-the-art IT grade infrastructure at BIT Sindri Campus, 
Dhanbad (Jharkhand). The centre provides services to IT/ITeS industry & startups/entrepreneurs 
of the region by offering Statutory services, Incubation services, High Speed Data 
Communication (HSDC) services, cyber security services, project management & consultancy 
services, IT managed services/co-location services and startup promotion services.
